title: Negative numbers: different signs make negative
metacognition_prompt: Before you start, what single skill is this repair problem checking?

source_reference.notes: Called by Q-003 Q003_MIXED_SIGN_SELECTION. Atomicity=num.negative_numbers; Scenario=Called by Q-003 Q003_MIXED_SIGN_SELECTION; Surface variation=yes; No new vocab=yes; Steps=1-2. Edexcel pivot metadata applied.

problem_text: Choose the signs: two numbers multiply to a negative number and add to a positive number.
student_prompt: Answer this short repair question. Keep your working brief.

error_category_mapping.diagnostic_sentence: If the smaller number is made positive, the product condition is handled but the sum sign is reversed. Mixed-sign factor pairs need a size check as well as a sign check.

hint_ladder.title: Opposite signs
hint_ladder.prompt: A negative product means the two signs are different. The positive sum tells you which number should carry the positive sign.

hint_ladder.title: Larger value
hint_ladder.prompt: With different signs, compare sizes. The larger absolute value controls whether the final sum is positive or negative.

hint_ladder.title: Sign placement
hint_ladder.prompt: A common slip is making the smaller number positive, which makes the sum negative instead of positive.

hint_ladder.title: Mixed-sign rule
hint_ladder.prompt: For a negative product, use opposite signs; for the sum sign, give the larger number that sign. Apply it here; do not copy.

common_errors: uses the previous larger problem instead of this repair skill
expected_solution_steps.diagnostic_sentence: This repair focuses on deciding which of the two opposite-signed numbers controls the sign of the final sum.
